First deep pass for GW5, run the same day GW5 waivers processed and the squad became final (deadline tomorrow 17:30 UTC). Roughly 25 searches across every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus predicted-lineup and press-conference searches for all eight GW5 fixtures touching the squad. Six of fifteen (Bogle, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Marmoush, Strand Larsen, Haaland) clear the bar for 'start' on permitted sources; the rest are 'likely' only because no permitted outlet has yet published this weekend's confirmed team news, not because of any real doubt - most searches surfaced only predicted-XI aggregators (Sports Mole, fotmob, RotoWire, Squawka, SI.com and similar), which are not permitted sources and were discarded even where they matched what a permitted source separately confirmed. Genuine finds: Gvardiol and Haaland were both left out entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich, confirmed on mancity.com as pure rotation with both expected back Sunday against Sunderland - worth flagging since a blank cup appearance could otherwise misread as an injury; Bogle was voted Newcastle's own Hisense Player of the Match after Monday's goal; Vuskovic scored his first Brighton goal against Leeds; and Strand Larsen kept his place for tonight's Europa League opener with Mateta still out. Ajayi's hamstring situation could not be resolved either way on a permitted source - Sky Sports' own 22 August lineup has him starting and scoring, but nothing since has been published on a permitted outlet, so he sits at 'likely' rather than 'start' pending this weekend's actual team news.
